Key concerns: API compatibility, eval parity (answers identical enough), latency under 200ms p50 for chat use case, and SOC2/KMS controls. topics: Compatibility OpenAI APIs vs Redwood endpoints
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:15 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood Solutions), Tom Reynolds (Proxima CTO), Priya Shah (Proxima ML), Lucas Nguyen (Proxima Security), Aisha Carter (Proxima DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): Proxima wants to move off OpenAI for cost predictability and data control; interested in Dedicated or Private. Concerned about eval parity and latency impact. Wants security docs and runbook.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE for your region. Quick intros?
[00:08] Tom: Hey Jordan, Tom Reynolds, CTO at Proxima. We've got Priya, Lucas, and Aisha on the line.
[00:12] Priya: Hi all, Priya here, ML eng, I'm leading the migration proofs.
[00:16] Jordan: Awesome. Maya, Liam, you want to intro?
[00:18] Maya: Yeah hi, Maya Patel, SE, I work on performance and migration — I usually run the POCs. Liam O'Connor, solutions - I'll help with architecture.
[00:26] Jordan: Great. Quick agenda: 1) understand current OpenAI usage and blockers, 2) compatibility questions (we often hear v-ELLM and TGI stuff), 3) security/ops, and 4) next steps + POC. Sound good?
[00:36] Tom: Yep that's what we're after. We want to reduce costs and have better control for data retention and audit.

[02:05] Priya: To start, we currently use OpenAI for chat generation and embeddings. It's a mix — some few-shot chat prompts, some single-turn generation. Roughly 30M tokens/month. Latency p50 around 250ms on OpenAI for our shorter prompts, p90 creeps up. Cost is starting to be material.
[02:28] Jordan: 30M tokens, got it. Are you using streaming responses for chat?
[02:33] Aisha: Yes streaming for the UI, we also do embedding calls for search and reranking.
[02:40] Lucas: Security-wise we need SOC 2 type II, encryption at rest with customer-controlled KMS, and SSO via SAML. Also audit logs retention for 1 year.
[02:52] Jordan: That aligns with our common asks; Redwood Dedicated supports VPC private deployment, KMS integrations, and audit logs. We'll share SOC2 docs and our support SLAs.

[05:10] Maya: On the compatibility side, most teams ask 'will our prompts get the same output on Redwood as on OpenAI' — that tends to be about model variant and tokenization. We map identical model families where possible; sometimes there are differences because of decoding defaults and sampling seeds.
[05:28] Priya: Important for us is eval parity. We run automated evals across 2k prompt pairs and need the numbers to be within a small delta. What's your process?
[05:39] Maya: We usually run a side-by-side eval on Dedicated using the same model family. If you're on OpenAI GPT-4-style family, we can either host a compatible open checkpoint or run the Redwood-verified variant. We also provide a benchmarking harness and metric spreadsheet.
[05:55] Tom: We heard about vLLM — is that what you run under the hood? And TGI? There's a lot of discussion in our infra team.
[06:05] Liam: good question — we support multiple runtimes. For Dedicated we optimize the serving runtime; it's not just vanilla vLLM or TGI — we use a GPU-optimized engine that handles KV cache, batching, and quantization. But we can run vLLM or TGI-style stacks if customers want parity testing.
[06:26] Priya: So there might be small behavioral differences; are there knobs to tune decoding to match exact outputs?
[06:32] Maya: We expose decoding params and can match temperature/penalty/top_p etc. Determinism is trickier — floating point and kernel-level differences can cause drift. For strict determinism, we'd recommend running the same binary/runtime, but in practice for evaluations we aim for functional parity rather than bit-exact outputs.

[09:00] Tom: Latency is big — our p50 target for chat is <200ms. Currently p50 is 250 on OpenAI for our median prompt size. Can Redwood Dedicated hit that?
[09:12] Maya: Depends on model size and sequence length. For smaller context models and good batching, we regularly see p50s under 150ms on Dedicated for <512 token sequences. We'll run benchmarks with your prompt distribution. Also placement matters — we can colocate in a cloud region closer to your users.
[09:28] Aisha: Network egress and VPC peering — we need to keep traffic on private links. Can Dedicated be deployed in our VPC?
[09:35] Liam: Yes Dedicated supports VPC peering and private connectivity, plus on-prem options if you require it. We'll share network diagrams.

[12:10] Lucas: About keys and encryption — we need customer-managed keys for model input data in transit and at rest, plus HSM for secrets. Do you support bringing your own keys?
[12:21] Jordan: Yes, KMS integrations and customer-managed keys are supported on our Private offering and can be configured for Dedicated via enterprise contracts. For Hosted we offer encryption but not always customer-managed KMS in the default plan — we'll clarify in the doc.

[15:45] Priya: Regarding model variants, we currently call OpenAI gpt-4o and gpt-4-mini for cheaper inference. Can Redwood host those exact checkpoints?
[15:58] Maya: We don't host closed checkpoints. We host open variants and Redwood-verified models which mimic the behaviour. For gpt-4-style, we work with compatible open checkpoints where possible and will surface any differences in the eval. Sometimes customers get better cost/latency tradeoffs by switching to a quantized variant.
[16:22] Priya: OK, so eval parity testing is a must for us.

[18:00] Jordan: On pricing — big picture: Hosted is usage-based, Dedicated is committed capacity (monthly/annual) with predictable throughput. For Dedicated we give you reserved GPU pools, and you can configure autoscale/burst. We'll send a sample pricing sheet with per-token equivalent and committed commit levels.
[18:22] Tom: What's typical commit for customers our size (30M tokens/month)?
[18:28] Jordan: It varies; some customers with similar usage start with a mid-tier node count that covers baseline and use burst for peak. The POC benchmark will give a better projection.

[20:05] Priya: About the actual migration — do you have tools to replay OpenAI logs and validate outputs?
[20:15] Maya: Yes we have a migration runbook: ingest a sample of your OpenAI response logs, replay them against Dedicated, and produce side-by-side diffs and metric deltas. We'll share the script and the benchmark sheet.
[20:28] Priya: Sweet. We'll need that. Also, how do you handle embeddings comparison? We use semantic search heavily and need embedding vector parity or at least close cosine similarity.
[20:40] Maya: For embeddings we can host the same model family if available. If not exact, we'll compute cosine deltas across your eval set and show recall/precision impact on your downstream search. Usually small vector shifts don't break search if the embedding quality is similar.

[23:10] Tom: What about inference runtime choices — vLLM vs TGI — our infra team loves vLLM for low-latency, but we've seen issues with concurrency. Any recommendations?
[23:24] Liam: vLLM is great when configured right, but out-of-the-box deployments need tuning. Our runtime optimizes kernel selection, continuous batching, and KV cache management; we've benchmarked against vLLM and TGI — they each have tradeoffs. For Dedicated we'll pick the optimal runtime per model and workload. We'll share our comparison notes.

[25:55] Lucas: Security review — we need pen-test reports, SOC2, and details on logging. Also, does Redwood provide per-request audit logs?
[26:07] Jordan: Yes per-request audit logs and tracing hooks; retention windows are configurable for Dedicated/Private. We'll include pen-test summaries and SOC2 paperwork in the security packet.

[28:45] Priya: Operationally, can we route certain traffic to Hosted for burst and fall back to Dedicated? We want graceful degradation if our Dedicated pool is exhausted.
[28:58] Maya: Absolutely — smart routing policies support that: we can route by region, cost, or latency, and there's an auto-fallback to Hosted or alternative model variants. It's a common pattern for customers moving from Hosted to Dedicated.

[31:15] Tom: What about model updates and rollouts — we need canarying.
[31:22] Liam: Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B tests and automatic rollback based on error rate or quality regressions. You can pin model versions per route.

[33:05] Priya: For the POC, what's the minimum setup we need?
[33:12] Maya: Minimal POC: 1) supply 500-1,000 representative prompts/responses, 2) give us a target latency/cost goal, 3) provide a small subset of logs for replay, and 4) designate a security contact for signing an NDA for any sensitive data. We'll provision a Dedicated test pool for 2 weeks to run side-by-side benchmarks.
[33:36] Tom: Timeline? We're hoping to decide within three weeks.
[33:41] Jordan: We can turn around the POC in 7-10 business days after we get prompts and access, so that aligns.

[36:00] Priya: A couple of nitty-gritty questions: tokenization differences and stop sequence handling — we've had issues where outputs truncated differently across runtimes.
[36:12] Maya: Yep that's a known issue; we provide tokenization docs and we can match stop sequences and trimming logic. We'll also run the same decoding library to minimize divergence where possible.

[38:50] Lucas: About compliance — do you support role-based access control and SSO? We use Okta and need SCIM provisioning ideally.
[38:59] Jordan: Yes SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning for user management are supported for Dedicated/Private. We'll include the integration guide.

[41:20] Aisha: Network egress costs — if we peer with Dedicated in our AWS account, how is egress handled?
[41:30] Liam: Typically egress is handled differently depending on setup; for VPC peering you minimize public egress but there are still cloud-provider charges sometimes — we'll include a network cost note.

[43:10] Priya: Any gotchas with long context lengths and KV cache behaviour? We have threads where context hits 4k tokens.
[43:20] Maya: For long contexts we leverage KV cache and selective caching. Sequence length affects memory and latency; we can recommend quantization profiles and model splits. We'll simulate your distribution in the POC.

[45:55] Tom: Ok this is super helpful. Let's recap next steps quickly.
[46:02] Jordan: Recap — Jordan sends pricing + Dedicated SKU + sample contract language; Maya shares migration runbook, benchmark sheet, and runtime comparison notes; Proxima provides eval prompts and logs; schedule POC for week of 2026-03-09. Anything to add?
[46:20] Priya: Please include embedding evaluation guidance.
[46:24] Maya: Noted.
[46:28] Lucas: Send security contact — I'll be the primary and will follow up with SSO details.
[46:33] Lucas: Also please share pen-test reports.
[46:37] Jordan: Will do.

[48:00] Tom: One final question — if we need an on-prem/private deployment, what's the rough lead time?
[48:07] Liam: Private or on-prem is longer — typically 6-10 weeks depending on network approvals and hardware procurement. For Dedicated in cloud it's much faster.

[49:30] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[49:35] Jordan: Thanks — we'll send the materials by Friday.
[49:39] Maya: I'll follow up with the runbook and spreadsheet.
[49:43] Tom: Appreciate it.
[49:45] Aisha: Thanks all.
